clue.text: Office chat about the letters

indicators.note: going about means turning around, so the word for chat is read backwards

blocks.note: a post is an office or appointment
gab is idle chatter

explanation.surface: Colleagues gossiping about the mail that arrived at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' looks like a workplace, but here it is a job or appointment, as in holding office.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbag is the collective mail a newspaper or public figure receives, so it stands for the letters.

clue.text: I'm standing in purplish brown lava, turned to stone

indicators.note: in a down clue standing means upright, so the word is read from the bottom up
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: puce is a dark purplish-brown colour
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone standing in dark lava as it hardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is the light porous rock formed when frothy lava cools and solidifies.

clue.text: Former capital (SA) I left abruptly

indicators.note: abruptly means cut short, so the last letter of that word is chopped off

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
someone who has left has gone

explanation.surface: A traveller recalls quitting an old South African capital in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: (SA) seems to name South Africa, but the letters are used just as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saigon was the capital of South Vietnam until 1975, when it was renamed Ho Chi Minh City.

clue.text: Not seeing clearly, you once got into bed early at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled
got into means went inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: ye is the old form of you
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tired sailor who turned in early on board ship still wakes up groggy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary-eyed describes eyes dim and unfocused from tiredness, so the person cannot see clearly.

clue.text: Queen comes back in to receive welcome

indicators.note: coming back means going the opposite way, so the letters are reversed
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to get is to receive
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch returns to a royal reception.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet someone is to welcome them on arrival.

clue.text: Spy soon replaced retiring agent

indicators.note: letters that are replaced are put back in a different order
retiring means drawing back, so the word for agent goes backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a rep is a sales agent or representative

explanation.surface: An espionage tale: a spy is swiftly swapped out for an agent who is stepping down.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooper pries into others' affairs, which is what a spy does, so the noun matches.

clue.text: Most appropriate to appear in case clutching one

indicators.note: clutching means holding tight, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: to seem is to appear
lest means in case, as in 'lest we forget'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Advice on looking right, perhaps for a court case, while holding something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case' looks like a container signal, but it is a block in its own right: the old word lest.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly means proper or fitting, so the seemliest thing is the most appropriate.

clue.text: Just short of 50, 10 stone

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the letter for that number is taken out

blocks.note: just and only both mean merely
L is the Roman numeral 50
X is the Roman numeral 10

explanation.surface: A weight reading: someone at just under fifty is ten stone.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, 14 pounds; here it means a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Got better under expert

indicators.note: in a down clue under means placed below, so that piece comes second

blocks.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
someone who got better was cured

explanation.surface: A patient recovered while in the care of a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got better' reads as one phrase meaning recovered; it splits into the definition and the cure.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure something is to obtain it, so procured means got.

clue.text: Cavalier king beheaded stalwart supporter

indicators.note: beheaded means the head is cut off, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: R is short for rex, king
a loyalist is a staunch supporter

explanation.surface: A Civil War scene: a Cavalier, a king's executed and faithful follower.
explanation.walkthrough: Cavaliers backed Charles I in the English Civil War, and he was indeed beheaded, which makes the surface read as history.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cavaliers were the supporters of the Crown in the English Civil War, that is, royalists.

clue.text: Miss West's heard about source of meal

indicators.note: heard tells us to go by the sound of the words, not their spelling

blocks.note: Mae West was the American film star, so Miss West is Mae, and Mae's is said the same as the grain

explanation.surface: Something Mae West reportedly said about where her food comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word here: the clue says what is heard about the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is ground into cornmeal, so the cereal crop is a source of meal.

clue.text: All English extremely stiff

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
very and extremely both intensify
a stiff is slang for a corpse, a dead body

explanation.surface: A complaint that every English person is terribly formal and starchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stiff' reads as an adjective with 'extremely', but it is the slang noun for a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: Everybody means every person, the whole group, which is what 'all' means used as a pronoun.

clue.text: Rich altos arranged liberal accommodation for singers

indicators.note: arranged suggests putting things into a new order, as music is arranged

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Wealthy contraltos have been given generous lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' fits the musical surface but is the anagram signal; 'liberal' only supplies its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir stall is the seat in a church chancel where choristers sit, so it houses singers.

clue.text: Head-to-head encounter unsettled Labour leader

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of the party name is used

blocks.note: a bill that is unsettled is still due
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A political story about a confrontation that rattled the Labour party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' reads as a politician, but it simply means the first letter of Labour. Labour is a major British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a fight between two people, a one-on-one contest.

clue.text: Forecaster pulling orator's leg

indicators.note: pulling means tugging out of shape, so the letters are distorted

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller is having a joke at a speechmaker's expense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulling someone's leg' is the idiom for teasing, but here pulling is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrologer claims to predict future events from the stars, so is a kind of forecaster.

clue.text: Favourites in form — trainer takes return flight

indicators.note: a return trip goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a teacher trains pupils
a flight of stairs is a set of steps

explanation.surface: Racing talk: the favourites are in good form, and the trainer flies home.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing words (favourites, form, trainer) all point to horses; a form is also a school class, and the flight is a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: Teacher's pets are the pupils a teacher favours, and a form is a British school class.

clue.text: Naivety ruled out in metropolis

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a metropolis is a big city
taken as written

explanation.surface: Innocence is outlawed in the big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruled out' reads as one phrase meaning excluded, but 'out' is the anagram signal on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Credulity is readiness to believe things too easily, which is naivety.

clue.text: Great king's daughter lacking company out of doors

indicators.note: lacking means without, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: Alfred the Great was a king of Wessex
D is short for daughter
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A king's daughter, with no one to keep her company, goes outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco, from Italian, means in the open air, so out of doors.

clue.text: More safe cracking causing alarm

indicators.note: cracking means breaking open, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Burglars breaking into more strongboxes is setting off alarms.
explanation.walkthrough: Safe-cracking and alarms make a burglary; 'cracking' acts on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fearsome is frightening, so it causes alarm in those who face it.

clue.text: Editor-elect's strange means of finding fiction?

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring hyphen and apostrophe

explanation.surface: A newspaper's incoming editor has an odd way of tracking down novels.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiction suggests novels on an editor's desk; here it means untruths, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Polygraphs are machines meant to expose lies, and a lie is a fiction in the sense of a made-up story.

clue.text: Stubborn chap keeps turning up to fix unit

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one piece sits within the other
in a down clue turning up means read from the bottom, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: a mule is an obstinate person
to do a job is to fix it, as in doing up a house

explanation.surface: An obstinate man keeps showing up to repair something.
explanation.definitionFit: A module is a self-contained unit, of a course, a spacecraft or a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Data, including university's rank

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: stats is short for statistics, data
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Figures that include a university's league table position.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is standing or position in a hierarchy, which is what rank means.

clue.text: Hearts of pirate crew not widely known

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only middle letters are kept

blocks.note: the two central letters of the word
the two central letters of the word

explanation.surface: The inner feelings of a band of buccaneers remain a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is uncommon, seldom met, so it is not widely known.

clue.text: Cuff led to a tailored garment

indicators.note: tailored means cut and reshaped, so the letters are refashioned

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sleeve cuff was the starting point for a made-to-measure item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The tailoring surface is so apt that 'tailored garment' looks like the definition; 'tailored' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A duffel coat is a hooded woollen overcoat with toggles, an item of outer clothing.

clue.text: Meat served in Raffles Hotel

indicators.note: served in suggests something presented inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A dish on the menu at Singapore's famous Raffles Hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Flesh is the soft tissue of an animal, and meat is the flesh eaten as food.

clue.text: Amphibian from west caught in snare

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a net is a snare or trap
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: A creature from the west has been trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is a small salamander, an amphibian living partly in water.

clue.text: Limit of main route certain to be announced first

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word counts by its sound

blocks.note: sure means certain, and in many accents it is said like the edge of the sea
a line is a route, as a railway line

explanation.surface: A transport notice: the boundary of the main route is sure to be published soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like 'principal', but it is the poetic word for the sea; 'first' places the sound-alike before the route.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is an old word for the open sea, and a shoreline is where the sea stops.

clue.text: Spare grand member of the family

blocks.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Asking whether a well-off relative could lend some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' reads as a verb asking for something, but it is the adjective meaning lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare as an adjective describes a lean, thin build, as does gaunt, which suggests a bony look.

clue.text: Surplus tax changing hands in public

indicators.note: changing hands means right is swapped for left, so the letter for right becomes the letter for left

blocks.note: over means left over, in surplus
to tax someone's patience is to try it

explanation.surface: A financial report: excess tax revenue being transferred to new owners in public.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'hands' are right and left: the R of the word for tax is swapped for an L.
explanation.definitionFit: Done overtly means done openly, not concealed, which is acting in public.

clue.text: Tackle difficulty Democrat avoided

indicators.note: avoided means kept out, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: hardness is difficulty
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: Deal with a problem that a political party member ducked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' reads as a verb about confronting a problem, but it is the noun for gear or equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is gear, including the straps and fittings of a horse, which is what a harness is.
